summary.text: A 31-year-old mother presented at 36 5/7 weeks of gestation with fever reaching 38.8°C and whole abdominal pain, had upper abdominal tenderness, leukocytosis with a left shift and mildly elevated CRP, and active labor with breech presentation requiring emergency cesarean section. Her older daughter had been clinically diagnosed with an enterovirus infection.

A late preterm female infant (GA 36 5/7 weeks, birth weight 2,555 g, Apgar 9 and 9) was admitted for transient tachypnea of the newborn with a normal initial CBC and CRP, received empiric ampicillin and gentamicin, and was weaned to room air by the third day of life.

On day 3 she deteriorated with fever of 38.3°C, apnea and bradycardia, with increased work of breathing, cyanosis, bilateral rales, ecchymosis over both legs, hepatosplenomegaly and bilateral lung field haziness on chest radiograph. Enterovirus PCR was positive and sequencing confirmed E-11.

She progressed to fulminant sepsis with multiorgan failure, hemorrhage-hepatitis syndrome, DIC, respiratory failure, severe hypotension, seizures and anuric acute kidney injury, treated with intubation, mechanical ventilation, vasoactive infusions, vitamin K1, fresh frozen plasma, platelets and CVVH, then IVIG 1g/kg and methylprednisolone pulse therapy.

Refractory shock was attributed to acute myocarditis based on echocardiography (global myocardial dysfunction, LVEF 45.5%, pericardial effusion) and troponin-I rising from 0.016 to 9.228 ng/mL. The ECMO team judged her not a suitable candidate; after family discussions a decision was made for withdrawal of life support and she died on the sixth day of life.
